The latest update is out from Cimentas Izmir Cimento Fabrikasi Turk A.S. ( (TR:CMENT) ).

Cimentas reported consolidated total assets of roughly TL 31.7 billion at 30 June 2026, slightly down from TL 33.0 billion at year-end 2025, as cash and cash equivalents fell sharply despite higher inventories and continued investment in fixed assets and investment property. Equity attributable to the parent slipped to about TL 18.45 billion from TL 18.64 billion, while total liabilities declined to TL 8.13 billion, leaving the company still strongly equity-funded but with rising deferred tax liabilities.

Operationally, the group swung to a net loss of TL 339.6 million for the first half of 2026 from a TL 326.5 million profit a year earlier, even though revenue more than doubled to TL 197.4 million and gross profit rose, as general and marketing expenses, fair value losses on investment property, heavy finance costs and a large net monetary position loss outweighed operating gains. Operating cash flow was a negative TL 1.77 billion, reflecting working capital outflows and inflation effects, while investment and financing cash flows were also negative; together these trends signal mounting pressure on liquidity and cash generation, with implications for shareholders and creditors despite the firm’s still-solid capital base.

More about Cimentas Izmir Cimento Fabrikasi Turk A.S.

Cimentas Izmir Cimento Fabrikasi Turk A.S. operates in the cement and building materials industry, producing cement and related construction inputs for the Turkish market and potentially for export. The company’s consolidated statements show it controls significant property, plant and equipment and investment properties, reflecting a capital-intensive manufacturing base geared to construction demand.

Its business is sensitive to domestic construction cycles, energy and input costs, and financing conditions. The presence of non-controlling interests indicates group structures and minority holdings, while sizeable deferred tax liabilities and right-of-use assets suggest exposure to changing tax and lease-accounting environments that can affect reported profitability and leverage metrics.

The latest announcement is out from Gold Terra Resource ( (TSE:YGT) ).

Gold Terra Resource Corp. has begun drilling on Zone 103N, the northern extension of the Campbell Shear within the historic Con Mine area, aiming to expand its recently announced 2026 inferred mineral resource of 595,000 ounces of gold. The zone is seen as a key contributor to a potential restart of the Con Mine and will feed into a Preliminary Economic Assessment expected by the end of 2026.

The company has also secured three new mineral claims, including YGT-2, which covers the northern extension of the Campbell Shear where any additional ounces will be 100% owned by Gold Terra. Supporting these plans, Gold Terra recently raised about C$9.2 million, with most of the funds allocated to drilling at Zone 103N, historical tailings work, and the Yellorex technical program.

Upcoming activities include extending drilling on Zone 103N, initiating drilling on historical Con Mine tailings in August 2026, and starting Yellorex drilling and metallurgical sampling in September 2026. These programs are intended to add resources and technical data to underpin the planned economic assessment and strengthen the company’s position in the Yellowknife gold camp.

data.description:

Haiki+ S.P.A. ( (IT:HIK) ) has issued an announcement.

SG Holding S.r.l. has announced a voluntary full public tender offer for all remaining ordinary shares of Haiki+ S.p.A. traded on Euronext Growth Milan, excluding the 56.10% stake it already owns. The offer is structured under Italian securities law and aims to consolidate ownership while complying with the rules set by CONSOB and Borsa Italiana.

The bid covers up to 59,674,488 shares, including potential new shares from warrant exercises, at a price of €0.90 per share, cum dividend. This represents a premium of 52.66% over the last closing price and 66.16% over the six‑month average, and is expressly intended to secure the delisting of Haiki+ from Euronext Growth Milan, signaling a move toward a closely held structure with reduced public market obligations for the company.

The offer also formalizes the role of Sostenya Group and affiliated Colucci family entities as parties acting in concert with SG Holding under Italian law. For existing minority shareholders, the proposed premium offers an exit at significantly above recent trading levels, but if successful, the transaction will remove Haiki+ from the public market, potentially limiting future liquidity and public price discovery for investors who do not tender.

More about Haiki+ S.P.A.

Haiki+ S.p.A. is an Italian company whose ordinary shares are admitted to trading on Euronext Growth Milan, a multilateral trading facility managed by Borsa Italiana. The company is part of a shareholder structure headed by SG Holding S.r.l. and ultimately controlled by Sostenya Group S.r.l., with stakes held by entities linked to the Colucci family.

The ownership chain includes SG Holding as the immediate holder of a majority stake in Haiki+, while Sostenya Group, Vegvisir, Vulcana, Neutral and their ultimate individual shareholders are deemed to act in concert. No single shareholder currently exercises legal control over Sostenya Group under Italian corporate law, reflecting a dispersed yet coordinated ownership structure around Haiki+.

Haiki+ operates within the Italian small-cap market segment served by Euronext Growth Milan, which typically hosts growth-oriented companies. Its listing on this venue subjects it to the regulatory framework overseen by CONSOB and Borsa Italiana, shaping the procedures and disclosure obligations around corporate actions such as tender offers and potential delistings.

Winamp Group has announced that Maxximum SRL, its reference shareholder controlled by CEO Alexandre Saboundjian, has acquired from Hexagon Capital Fund the bonds issued under the second tranche of a 2025 financing agreement. The deal concerns only the transfer of bond ownership and is structured to address Belgian takeover rules following a temporary crossing of the 50% shareholding threshold after a February 2026 capital increase.

Winamp Group is a digital music company that owns the Winamp platform, copyright management firm Bridger, music licensing service Jamendo and digital radio bouquet Hotmix. The group focuses on empowering artists, songwriters and independent musicians with tools for rights management, monetization, licensing and fan engagement across its platforms, targeting the global online music and audio market.

Through Winamp, the company offers a creator-focused platform and player designed to help artists manage their catalogs, grow audiences and maximize revenue. Jamendo supports a global community of independent artists via music sharing and commercial licensing, while Bridger simplifies copyright collection for songwriters and Hotmix delivers more than sixty curated, free thematic digital radio stations for music listeners worldwide.
